Presenter quick guide

Use the top tabs as the session outline. Select a saved policy, play or scrub its day, then reveal the stage-specific result. The blank grid reading at 00:00 means no policy action has happened yet. Playback stops at 24:00; use Reset day to replay. Every replay uses the same five-household scenario.

  • Space: play/pause; ← / →: step; R: reveal.
  • Introduction: click a house to see trip times, ordered preferences, permission, demand, solar, and the home-only reference bill. Scroll down for the demand/solar and shared price charts. The reference excludes EV charging, so the trip is missed. After showing the cards, press Show grid with EVs idle for its 24-hour grid curve and optional replay. Back to household cards resets the Introduction. Press Start comparing choices to begin the justice discussion.
  • Epistemic: start with grid and travel priorities. Use Why Pareto? to inspect 15 example points. The two named buttons highlight a near-unchanged-grid household gain and an all-measures improvement. Red points connect to green points that improve both plotted stakeholder results; the first named pair has a tiny command-mismatch increase. Then reveal the full Pareto front; click any green point to replay it.
  • Distributive: each percentage is missing battery energy divided by that home's own trip-energy need.
  • Recognitional: begin with the 1:1 policy to reveal whose plans it already follows. Then compare fully respecting the separate household plans, balancing them with the grid, and sharing burdens across homes. Average plan alignment is the mean of the five household bars. The combined policy makes those bars almost equal but lowers their average; the ideal plans do not coordinate the grid. In “What matters after the trip?”, click a household to see its second priority beside trip-energy shortfall for these four policies.
  • Fixed indicators remain in the simulation; the right panel changes what justice question is being examined.

Full timings, prompts, indicators, and data provenance are in JustNexus_Offline_Demo/README.md.
EPISTEMIC JUSTICE

Who decides the compromise?

The households and grid have different goals. Each dot is a tested controller; lower is better on both axes. Explore seven compromises, inspect the full front, or use Why Pareto? to compare more green and red examples. Click any point to see its two outcomes.
